phases.name: Define the multilingual processing contract
phases.description: Translate each requested NLP capability and numerical target into separate measurable acceptance criteria.

phases.name: Create real-time and batch intake paths
phases.description: Provide a protected API, durable batch handoff, shared normalization, and explicit model tasks for every requested analysis.

phases.name: Connect entity and document analysis
phases.description: Keep real-time requests short, let batch jobs use durable object references, run dependent extraction in order, and aggregate the full result.

phases.name: Measure quality, latency, and throughput
phases.description: Observe both service paths and choose language-aware quality gates and independent scaling policies.

steps.title: Preserve every requested NLP capability and target
steps.content: Problem: Design a Natural Language Processing Pipeline. Description: Design an NLP pipeline that processes unstructured text through entity extraction, relation extraction, sentiment analysis, topic modeling, and text classification at scale. Frozen metadata: difficulty Medium; category ML - NLP; estimated time 45-60 minutes. Functional requirements: Extract named entities (people, organizations, locations); Identify relationships between entities; Classify documents into categories; Perform sentiment and opinion analysis; Extract key phrases and topics; Handle multiple languages; Process structured and unstructured text; Provide API for batch and real-time processing. Constraints: Entity extraction F1-score above 90%; Classification accuracy above 85%; Process 10k+ documents per hour in batch; Real-time processing under 500ms per document; Support at least 10 languages. Hints: Use transformer-based models (BERT, RoBERTa) for NER; Implement SpaCy for fast entity extraction; Use fine-tuned models per domain for accuracy; Implement text preprocessing (tokenization, normalization); Use BERTopic or LDA for topic modeling; Deploy models behind a FastAPI service. These are design inputs and targets, not measured results.

steps.title: Treat quality and capacity numbers as test gates
steps.content: Measure entity F1 and document classification accuracy by language and relevant domain, not only as a global average. Benchmark batch throughput on representative document lengths and language mixes. Measure real-time end-to-end latency from API ingress through response serialization; the brief does not specify payload size, traffic burst shape, or language distribution.

steps.title: Choose a shared multilingual preprocessing contract
steps.content: Normalize Unicode, preserve original text and offsets, detect or accept a declared language, and tokenize with a model-compatible versioned pipeline. Route to language and domain configurations without silently translating away entity spans or sentiment cues.

decision.question: How should the pipeline handle at least ten languages without erasing language-specific evidence?
decision.chosen: Use language-aware routing to multilingual transformer models such as XLM-R and domain-fine-tuned BERT/RoBERTa models, with spaCy as a fast baseline where language-level evaluation supports it.
decision.chosenReason: One multilingual entry contract can support a varied language mix while per-language evaluation reveals where a dedicated model or fallback is needed.

alternatives.option: Translate every input to one language before all analysis
alternatives.tradeoff: Translation can change entity boundaries, opinion nuance, and provenance, and adds latency.

alternatives.option: Use one unqualified model for every language
alternatives.tradeoff: Aggregate scores can conceal poor quality for less represented languages.

steps.phase: Create real-time and batch intake paths
steps.title: Expose one documented API for real-time and batch jobs
steps.content: Provide request validation, authentication, language hints, correlation IDs, and separate synchronous and batch submission contracts. A batch submission returns a job reference rather than holding an API connection open for the full corpus.

component.label: NLP API: Real-Time and Batch Submission
component.description: Protected API boundary for synchronous analysis and asynchronous document jobs.

properties.purpose: Validate and authenticate real-time analysis and batch job requests, attach trace and language context, and return a job reference for asynchronous submissions.

component.highlightReason: One API contract supports the requested batch and real-time modes while making their response behavior explicit.

steps.phase: Create real-time and batch intake paths
steps.title: Keep large batch documents and results in object storage
steps.content: Store batch inputs, manifests, and completed outputs durably with access controls, encryption, and an agreed retention policy. Pass object references through queues so large document bodies do not become queue payloads.

component.label: Batch Documents and NLP Results
component.description: Durable inputs, manifests, and result files for asynchronous processing.

properties.purpose: Store encrypted batch inputs, manifests, and outputs with controlled retention; queue only bounded document or object references.

component.highlightReason: Object references support large unstructured and structured batches without oversized messages.

steps.phase: Create real-time and batch intake paths
steps.title: Buffer batch work with bounded retries and visible lag
steps.content: Use a durable queue for batch job or chunk references, with idempotency keys, bounded retry policy, a dead-letter path, and oldest-message-age monitoring. Tune consumer concurrency to sustain the 10k+ documents-per-hour objective without exhausting downstream model capacity.

component.label: Durable Batch Work Queue
component.description: Replayable job references with bounded retries and consumer-lag signals.

properties.purpose: Buffer idempotent document or chunk references, bound retries, route exhausted work for review, and expose queue age and depth for throughput control.

component.highlightReason: A durable queue separates bulk arrivals from inference execution and makes batch backpressure observable.

steps.phase: Create real-time and batch intake paths
steps.title: Run batch chunks with checkpointed progress
steps.content: Claim bounded chunks, record job and chunk progress, and retry only idempotent work. Limit each worker's concurrency to protect shared model capacity and preserve per-document identity through the result aggregation step.

component.label: Batch Job Coordinator
component.description: Loads bounded chunks and tracks retryable batch progress.

properties.purpose: Load document references, track idempotent chunk progress, limit concurrency against model capacity, and persist per-document results and job completion state.

component.highlightReason: The worker makes batch retries and progress independent from the real-time request lifetime.

steps.phase: Create real-time and batch intake paths
steps.title: Normalize structured and unstructured text consistently
steps.content: Validate structured fields and extract text from supported unstructured inputs. Normalize Unicode and whitespace, preserve source offsets and metadata, tokenize with the selected model contract, identify language, and enforce a versioned allowlist of at least 10 supported languages. Route only to validated language/model pairs, and return or record an explicit unsupported-language outcome for inputs outside that allowlist.

component.label: Text Normalization and Language Router
component.description: Versioned normalization, tokenization, input validation, and language-aware routing for at least 10 supported languages.

properties.purpose: Handle structured and unstructured input, preserve offsets and provenance, normalize and tokenize text, resolve language, and route through a versioned registry containing at least 10 explicitly supported languages and compatible model versions.

component.highlightReason: A shared, versioned preprocessing boundary keeps batch and real-time model inputs consistent across at least 10 explicitly supported languages.

steps.phase: Create real-time and batch intake paths
steps.title: Extract people, organizations, and locations
steps.content: Run multilingual NER that emits entity type, confidence, source offsets, language, and model version. Evaluate F1 above 90% on representative language and domain slices; compare a fast spaCy path with transformer or fine-tuned alternatives rather than assuming one performs best everywhere.

component.label: Multilingual Named Entity Recognition
component.description: People, organization, and location spans with confidence and provenance.

properties.purpose: Extract person, organization, and location spans with type, confidence, language, model version, and preserved source offsets; benchmark F1 by language and domain.

component.highlightReason: Named entity spans and provenance are the explicit input to downstream relation extraction.

steps.phase: Create real-time and batch intake paths
steps.title: Extract typed relationships between identified entities
steps.content: Consume the document tokens and NER spans, then return typed relations linked to the source entities and text evidence. Preserve an explicit no-relation result rather than forcing a relation for every entity pair.

component.label: Entity Relation Extraction
component.description: Typed links between recognized entities with supporting text spans.

properties.purpose: Identify typed relationships from normalized text and NER spans; retain evidence offsets, confidence, language, and model version.

component.highlightReason: Explicit entity inputs make the dependency between named-entity and relationship extraction reviewable.

steps.phase: Create real-time and batch intake paths
steps.title: Classify documents against the agreed category taxonomy
steps.content: Return category labels and confidence using a versioned taxonomy. Measure accuracy above 85% on held-out, language-aware data and define what happens when confidence is low or a document belongs to an unseen category.

component.label: Document Classification
component.description: Versioned category predictions with confidence and fallback status.

properties.purpose: Assign taxonomy versioned category labels with confidence and explicit low-confidence or unknown-category outcomes; evaluate accuracy by language and domain.

component.highlightReason: The taxonomy and uncertainty behavior make the classification accuracy target measurable.

steps.phase: Create real-time and batch intake paths
steps.title: Analyze sentiment and opinion with language context
steps.content: Return polarity or opinion labels with confidence and language context. Retain the analyzed text evidence and distinguish neutral or ambiguous language from a confident positive or negative result.

component.label: Sentiment and Opinion Analysis
component.description: Language-aware sentiment outputs with confidence and evidence references.

properties.purpose: Analyze sentiment and opinion with language-aware confidence, evidence references, and an explicit uncertain or neutral result.

component.highlightReason: Separate sentiment output lets the pipeline measure opinion analysis without conflating it with topic or category labels.

steps.phase: Create real-time and batch intake paths
steps.title: Extract key phrases and document topics
steps.content: Produce key phrases and topic assignments with model or topic-model version. Compare BERTopic, LDA, or a domain-fine-tuned approach on the corpus and language mix; do not imply that all options have the same latency or multilingual quality.

component.label: Key Phrase and Topic Extraction
component.description: Document phrases and topic assignments with versioned model metadata.

properties.purpose: Extract key phrases and topics with language, corpus, and model-version metadata; evaluate BERTopic, LDA, or fine-tuned alternatives on representative data.

component.highlightReason: A distinct topic task makes the key-phrase and topic requirement independently observable.

steps.phase: Create real-time and batch intake paths
steps.title: Merge task outputs into a traceable document response
steps.content: Join NER spans, relations, categories, sentiment, and topics by document and request identity. Return per-task model versions, confidence, evidence offsets, warnings, and partial-failure status so the caller can distinguish missing analysis from an empty result.

component.label: NLP Result Aggregator
component.description: Combines independent analysis outputs and preserves per-task status.

properties.purpose: Join task outputs by document ID, retain task-level confidence, evidence, language and model versions, and report partial failures explicitly.

component.highlightReason: A single aggregation contract serves both API responses and durable batch result records.

steps.phase: Create real-time and batch intake paths
steps.title: Observe quality and service behavior by mode and language
steps.content: Monitor request latency, error and partial-result rates, queue age, document throughput, model version, language distribution, and quality signals when labels become available. Separate the real-time latency view from batch completion throughput.

component.label: NLP Quality and Operations Monitoring
component.description: Per-language model and service signals for online requests and batch jobs.

properties.purpose: Track per-language task quality when labels arrive, real-time latency, batch throughput and queue age, errors, partial results, and model versions.

component.highlightReason: Separate online and batch signals are necessary to evaluate their different targets.

steps.title: Send real-time requests through shared preprocessing
steps.content: The synchronous route passes bounded text and metadata to the shared preprocessing contract, with its deadline and trace context attached.

connection.label: Real-time text request
connection.description: Forward validated bounded input and request deadline to the shared normalization path.

steps.title: Submit batch jobs without occupying a synchronous request
steps.content: The API returns a job identifier after placing bounded job references on the asynchronous path. Clients can query or receive completion through the documented job contract.

connection.label: Batch job reference
connection.description: Enqueue idempotent job or chunk references for asynchronous processing.

steps.title: Persist batch input before queueing its manifest
steps.content: Store the batch documents and manifest, then submit their object references. This keeps queue messages bounded and allows a job to resume after worker failure.

connection.label: Batch input and manifest
connection.description: Persist large input before sending object references through the batch queue.

steps.title: Make stored manifests available to queued jobs
steps.content: Queue only the immutable manifest or object keys needed to load a batch. Avoid duplicating document bodies in the queue.

connection.label: Manifest reference
connection.description: Make stored batch references available to the asynchronous consumer.

steps.title: Dispatch batch references to bounded workers
steps.content: Workers claim jobs with an idempotency key and record progress before acknowledging completed chunks.

connection.label: Claimed batch work
connection.description: Deliver bounded work with retry and progress identity.

steps.title: Load the batch object by its manifest reference
steps.content: The worker reads the exact stored input version, preserving document IDs and source metadata for later aggregation.

connection.label: Versioned batch input
connection.description: Read the stored input and manifest referenced by the queued job.

steps.title: Reuse the same preprocessing rules for batch documents
steps.content: The worker submits bounded document chunks through the shared normalization, language, and tokenization version used by real-time requests.

connection.label: Batch document chunk
connection.description: Run batch input through the shared versioned preprocessing contract.

steps.title: Pass normalized, language-aware text to NER
steps.content: Preserve tokens, source offsets, language, and trace identity on the NER request.

connection.label: Tokens and language context
connection.description: Provide normalized text while retaining original evidence offsets and language.

steps.title: Run relation extraction over recognized entity spans
steps.content: The relation model receives entity spans and their document context, so each predicted relationship can refer back to identified people, organizations, and locations.

connection.label: Entity spans and context
connection.description: Use recognized entities as candidates for typed relation extraction.

steps.title: Retain entity results in the combined response
steps.content: Send entity types, offsets, confidences, and model version to the result join.

connection.label: Named entity results
connection.description: Attach typed entity spans and their provenance to the document response.

steps.title: Join relationships with their source entities
steps.content: Keep relation endpoints and supporting evidence linked to the same document and entity IDs.

connection.label: Entity relationships
connection.description: Join typed relation predictions and evidence with the recognized entity results.

steps.title: Run document categorization from normalized text
steps.content: Category classification can proceed independently of relation extraction once normalized language-aware text is available.

connection.label: Normalized document
connection.description: Send model-compatible text and language context to the category classifier.

steps.title: Add versioned category predictions to the result
steps.content: Retain taxonomy version, confidence, and low-confidence status with each category result.

connection.label: Document categories
connection.description: Join category predictions with taxonomy and confidence metadata.

steps.title: Analyze opinion in parallel with independent tasks
steps.content: Run sentiment analysis on the shared normalized input rather than waiting for relation extraction.

connection.label: Normalized document
connection.description: Send language-aware input to the independent sentiment task.

steps.title: Join sentiment with confidence and evidence references
steps.content: Keep opinion output distinct from category and topic results, including neutral or uncertain states.

connection.label: Sentiment and opinion
connection.description: Attach sentiment, confidence, and evidence metadata to the document result.

steps.title: Extract key phrases and topics from the shared input
steps.content: Run phrase and topic analysis as an independent task after normalization; apply its own batch or real-time resource policy if measured costs differ.

connection.label: Normalized document
connection.description: Send versioned text and language context to topic and phrase analysis.

steps.title: Include phrase and topic outputs in the response
steps.content: Attach phrase spans and topic assignments with the corpus and model version used to produce them.

connection.label: Key phrases and topics
connection.description: Join phrase and topic output with document and model-version metadata.

steps.title: Return real-time results through the API contract
steps.content: Return the combined response or a clearly marked partial result before the request deadline. Do not report a missing task response as an empty prediction.

connection.label: Combined analysis response
connection.description: Return task results, confidence, evidence, and partial status to the caller.

steps.title: Persist batch results by job and document identity
steps.content: Write completed batch results and per-document status to durable storage so clients can retrieve results after asynchronous processing.

connection.label: Batch outputs and status
connection.description: Persist completed results with job, document, language, and model-version identifiers.

steps.title: Measure end-to-end real-time behavior
steps.content: Emit request latency, language, task completion status, errors, and correlation IDs while respecting text privacy and retention policy.

connection.label: Online request telemetry
connection.description: Measure full-path latency, task status, and errors for synchronous traffic.

steps.title: Watch batch backlog and completed-document rate
steps.content: Track queue age, depth, retry count, and completed documents per hour separately from online latency.

connection.label: Batch lag and throughput
connection.description: Expose backlog, retries, and completion rate for the 10k+ documents-per-hour target.

steps.title: Attribute entity quality and latency to model versions
steps.content: When labeled evaluation or production feedback is available, attribute NER precision, recall, F1, and inference time to language, domain, and model version.

connection.label: NER quality and runtime
connection.description: Attribute language-level NER evidence and latency to the deployed model version.

steps.title: Measure relation extraction independently
steps.content: Monitor relation output validity, confidence, runtime, and model version so errors in entity detection can be separated from relation classification.

connection.label: Relation task signals
connection.description: Record relation-task runtime, status, and available quality feedback.

steps.title: Track classification accuracy by taxonomy and language
steps.content: Record taxonomy and model versions with labeled accuracy and low-confidence outcomes; review language slices before relying on a global score. Measure task runtime as part of the end-to-end real-time latency budget.

connection.label: Classification quality
connection.description: Attribute accuracy evidence and runtime to language, taxonomy, and model version.

steps.title: Watch sentiment drift and uncertain outputs
steps.content: Monitor language-level output distributions and uncertain cases, and review them against labeled opinion data instead of treating distribution shifts as proof of model failure. Measure task runtime as part of the end-to-end real-time latency budget.

connection.label: Sentiment task signals
connection.description: Record sentiment version, latency, uncertainty, and available evaluation evidence.

steps.title: Keep topic-model behavior visible by corpus version
steps.content: Track topic and phrase outputs with corpus and model versions, latency against the end-to-end real-time budget, and batch resource use; topic quality requires its own reviewed evaluation approach.

connection.label: Topic task signals
connection.description: Record topic and phrase runtime, model or corpus version, and reviewed quality signals.

steps.title: Keep dependent extraction ordered and independent tasks parallel
steps.content: Relation extraction depends on recognized entity spans. Classification, sentiment, and topics can run independently after shared preprocessing, subject to measured resource contention and the synchronous deadline.

decision.question: Which model tasks belong on the critical dependency chain?
decision.chosen: Run NER first and relation extraction over its entity spans; run classification, sentiment, and topic analysis in parallel from normalized text.
decision.chosenReason: This preserves the data dependency for relations and reduces avoidable serial work for independent document tasks.

alternatives.tradeoff: Unnecessary serial latency can consume the under-500ms real-time budget.

alternatives.option: Run relation extraction before entity recognition
alternatives.tradeoff: The relation task lacks the explicit entity spans this design uses as candidates.

steps.title: Scale the two workload modes against different signals
steps.content: Do not let a batch backlog consume every model worker needed by real-time traffic. Reserve or prioritize online capacity and cap batch concurrency using measured service time and queue age.

scaleTrigger.metric: Real-time end-to-end latency and batch oldest-job age/completed documents per hour
scaleTrigger.action: Scale online capacity to sustain the tested request profile; independently add bounded batch consumers when queue age rises, subject to model capacity and the 10k+ documents-per-hour target.
scaleTrigger.impact: Separating control signals protects the real-time latency objective while allowing batch throughput to grow without starving interactive requests.

steps.title: Gate model versions on language-level evidence
steps.content: Set evaluation data and release criteria before promoting model changes. Keep NER F1 and classification accuracy as separate metrics; success on one does not imply success on the other or in every supported language.

decision.question: What evidence is required before using a new multilingual model version?
decision.chosen: Require entity extraction F1 above 90% and classification accuracy above 85% on agreed representative language and domain slices, then verify the language coverage and latency budget before release.
decision.chosenReason: The explicit brief thresholds become testable gates, and sliced evaluation prevents strong languages from hiding weak ones.

alternatives.option: Promote when a single aggregate score passes
alternatives.tradeoff: A global score can mask a language-specific failure.

alternatives.option: Use model family or parameter count as the quality gate
alternatives.tradeoff: Architecture labels do not establish measured accuracy on this corpus.

steps.title: Verify throughput and latency with representative documents
steps.content: Benchmark at least 10 languages, representative structured and unstructured inputs, and realistic document lengths. Verify batch processing sustains 10k+ documents per hour and real-time processing remains under 500ms per document while returning all requested tasks or an explicit partial status. These are acceptance targets; this local walkthrough reports no performance or publication gate as passed.
